entrypoints.summary: The JPEG 2000 decoder's jp2_find_codestream function enters a nested atom scan and reads each nested header as two big-endian 32-bit fields.
A public 1,025-byte minimized ClusterFuzz testcase is linked by the maintainer patch to the JPEG2000 fuzzer finding.

affected_components.role: Nested JP2 atom scan; the patch inserts a header-availability break immediately before size and type reads.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The guard is inside jp2_find_codestream's nested atom scan and precedes atom2_size, atom2, and atom2_end assignment.
code_slices.vulnerable: Before the insertion, the nested scan proceeded directly to two bytestream2_get_be32u calls for atom2_size and atom2.

observability.channel: timeout or loss of decoder progress
negative_controls: No vulnerable/fixed run transcript is present.
The issue page available in the bundle is login-gated and provides no timeout configuration or trace.
observability.positive_marker: The patch explicitly identifies the corrected finding as an infinite loop.

preconditions: An affected FFmpeg build processes attacker-supplied JPEG 2000/JP2 content.
The content reaches the nested atom scan with an incomplete next header.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: 1,025-byte binary ClusterFuzz minimized testcase; detailed JP2 field layout is not established by the bundle.
trigger_steps.summary: Supply the public minimized JPEG 2000 testcase linked by the patch to the JPEG2000 fuzzer finding.

impact.attacker_capability: Cause an affected FFmpeg JPEG 2000 decode operation to loop indefinitely using the linked malformed testcase or an input reaching the same incomplete nested-header state.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through decoder non-termination while processing the malformed JPEG 2000 input.

causal_trace.summary: A minimized JPEG 2000 fuzzer input associated with issue 36666 reaches the JPEG2000 decoder's nested JP2 atom scan.
At a nested-atom loop boundary, fewer than eight bytes can remain even though the pre-fix code proceeds to consume the fixed-size nested atom size/type header.
The unguarded loop invokes bytestream2_get_be32u twice to obtain atom2_size and atom2; the maintainer labels the corrected behavior as an infinite loop.
The demonstrated outcome is decoder non-termination (infinite loop), which can deny processing availability for the supplied malformed input.

failure.operation: Unguarded nested-header reads with bytestream2_get_be32u in the jp2_find_codestream loop, associated by the patch with an infinite loop.

primary_invariant.statement: At least eight bytes must remain in the bytestream before a nested JP2 atom header's 32-bit size and 32-bit type are consumed.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Before the added loop-boundary check, the code read atom2_size and atom2 directly without first testing bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&s->g) for the eight-byte header.

quality.review_notes: The primary maintainer patch explicitly links the minimized testcase and labels the fix as an infinite-loop correction. The bundle has no accessible issue timeout transcript, vulnerable/fixed execution log, full pre-fix loop body, or demonstrated historical OSS-Fuzz build image; thus the precise no-progress transition and replay determinism remain unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: The decoder breaks out of the nested atom scan when fewer than eight bytes remain, before consuming either field of a nested atom header.
mitigation_classes: reject or stop parsing incomplete fixed-width nested headers

oss_fuzz.crash_state: A public minimized testcase is linked by the maintainer patch; no accessible OSS-Fuzz execution trace is present.
